runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current NPPF, Green Belt PPG, viability guidance and adopted London Plan readback with grey-belt/Golden-Rules tests kept separate from parcel release or permission.

sources.label: NPPF Section 13
sources.fact: Current national policy sets Green Belt tests and identifies circumstances where grey-belt development is not inappropriate if all paragraph 155 criteria are met.

sources.label: NPPF paragraph 155
sources.fact: Grey-belt status alone is insufficient: remaining-Green-Belt purpose, unmet need, sustainable location and Golden Rules where applicable must also be satisfied.

sources.label: NPPF Golden Rules
sources.fact: Major housing on relevant Green Belt/released land should contribute affordable housing, necessary infrastructure and accessible green space.

sources.label: NPPF paragraph 157
sources.fact: Until updated plan policies exist, the affordable contribution is 15 percentage points above the highest otherwise-applicable requirement, capped at 50%, with 50% default where none exists.

sources.label: GOV.UK Green Belt guidance
sources.fact: Updated 27 February 2025; grey-belt identification does not automatically mean allocation, release or approval.

sources.label: Green Belt assessment guidance
sources.fact: Authorities should produce a Green Belt assessment where relevant to identifying grey belt and reviewing boundaries.

sources.label: Green Belt accessible green-space guidance
sources.fact: Golden Rules green-space provision should consider safe access, active travel, public transport, nature recovery and long-term maintenance.

sources.label: GOV.UK Viability guidance
sources.fact: Updated 16 December 2025; site-specific viability should not be used to reduce Golden Rules contributions for relevant Green Belt development.

sources.label: London Plan Policy G2
sources.fact: Adopted London Plan protects Green Belt from inappropriate development and requires exceptional circumstances for boundary change through plan preparation/review.

sources.label: London Plan Policy G3
sources.fact: Metropolitan Open Land is afforded the same status and level of protection as Green Belt under the adopted London Plan.

sources.label: Current London Plan status
sources.fact: London Plan 2021 remains the current adopted planning framework for London.

sources.label: London Local Nature Recovery Strategy
sources.fact: LNRS is strategic nature-recovery evidence and does not by itself create a development permission or Green Belt release.

examples.result: Grey-belt identification alone is not treated as allocation, release or permission.
Paragraph 155 tests are checked cumulatively; no single criterion is treated as sufficient.
Golden Rules affordable-housing percentage is not assigned without the applicable development-plan baseline.
Site-specific viability is not used to discount Golden Rules where national guidance says it should not be.
London Policy G2 remains adopted context; emerging policy does not silently replace it.
MOL is not treated as ordinary open land; adopted G3 protection is retained.
LNRS priority context does not itself remove Green Belt/MOL policy tests.
No Green Belt/grey-belt candidate promotion occurs without exact polygon, policy relation and application-specific evidence.
